notes: Template (Inventory_Equip) does not match this owner at all -- weak cluster match. Read games/gs1/asm/0807a664.s directly: this is a party-wide inventory sanitation pass gated by a sentinel check on Data_02001078[0] (proceeds only if it already equals 0x6774, then re-stamps it), guarded by an unusual save/restore of two u16 values read from Data_02000240+0x220/+0x222 before the work and re-emitted (alongside two more reads from Data_02000240+0/+2) into a growing buffer at Data_02001078+2 that accumulates 2 bytes per inventory slot across ALL FOUR owners (0..3): for each owner, OwnerState_Get(owner)->inventory[0..13] is first copied out into that shared buffer, then each of the 14 slots is looked up via Func_08078414 and cleared to 0 unless its type byte (offset 2) equals 6, then the SAME 15-slot compact-non-zero-then-zero-fill algorithm documented in main:080788c4's dossier (Inventory_Remove) is run in place on inventory[0..14], and finally Func_08079ae8(owner)/Func_08077428(owner) are called before moving to the next owner. After all four owners, the two saved u16 values plus two more fields from Data_02000240 are appended to the same growing buffer, then Func_0807a628(0,16) and Func_08079358(0x02000438) are called. The whole function ends by unconditionally calling Func_0807808c(1) whether or not the sentinel check passed.

This is a large, multi-part owner (316 bytes, 7 saved registers, a nested owner-loop containing the same compaction algorithm as 080788c4 run per-owner, plus save/restore bookkeeping around it) worked as one best-effort direct-translation pass given the batch's per-owner budget, not iterated to convergence. The pass compiles and is roughly the right size (308B vs 316B) but wrong_instructions=159 out of roughly 154 total instructions -- i.e. more than half disagree, so this should be read as a structural sketch rather than a close candidate.

Specific known weaknesses in the current draft: (1) the exact semantics of the buffer being built at Data_02001078+2 (a 'growing pointer that survives the whole outer loop, incrementing by 2 per inventory slot across all four owners plus a few trailing fields') is inferred from the assembly's r8 register never resetting between owners, but the surrounding purpose (some kind of trade/transfer snapshot?) is not confirmed; (2) the two saved values (from Data_02000240+0x220/+0x222, read BEFORE the owner loop and written AFTER it) are modeled as plain locals, which is probably right but their meaning is unconfirmed; (3) whether Func_08078414's return value is genuinely dereferenced at byte offset +2 the same way as in 080788c4's sibling functions, or points to a different struct, is assumed rather than verified against a header.

Given the size of the gap, the most useful next step is treating this as a fresh, patient full pass (ideally re-deriving the r8-accumulator idiom and the sentinel-gated save/restore precisely) rather than incremental respelling from this draft.
